title: Enterprise Onboarding — Known Issues, Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Nadia Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the canonical procedures and reference material used by Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and SRE when onboarding enterprise customers. It covers: integration prerequisites, common known issues and workarounds, the escalation matrix and runbook for P0/P1/P2 incidents, and the QBR/health-check checklist we use to track adoption and risk.

Audience: Customer Success (CSMs), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support Engineers, Oncall SRE, and Sales engineering.

Goals:
- Ensure consistent and fast time-to-value during the first 90 days of an enterprise onboarding.
- Provide clear escalation paths to resolve customer-impacting incidents within SLA targets.
- Centralize known issues and mitigations to reduce ticket cycle time.
- Provide a repeatable QBR structure to measure health and drive adoption.

Owner & Contacts:
- Playbook owner: Nadia Patel (Customer Success)
- Primary escalation contact: Oncall SRE (via PagerDuty) — see Escalation Matrix below
- Slack channels: #cs-enterprise, #se-onboarding, #oncall-ops
- PagerDuty service: redwood-inference-prod-oncall
- Email for enterprise escalations: enterprise-escalations@redwood.ai

Integration checklist (pre-onboarding tasks):
1) Account and billing:
   - Confirm billing account is provisioned and customer has accepted contract terms.
   - Assign billing contacts and create billing role in console (Owner, Billing-Admin).
2) Access and IAM:
   - Create API key(s) with scoped permissions for integration testing.
   - For Private/Dedicated deployments, confirm VPN/VPC peering and firewall rules.
3) Network & Security:
   - Verify egress rules to the platform endpoints and ports 443/8443 are open.
   - For Private, validate KMS/HSM integration and key access tests.
4) Data residency & compliance:
   - Confirm region requirements and retention policy (if applicable).
5) Technical smoke test (run before handoff):
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deployments/test-generate 
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' 
     -d '{"input":"Hello world"}'
   - Validate response, check p95 latency < 500ms for small prompts.

Core integration items (configuration table):
| Item | Required | Owner | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|-------|
| API Key | Yes | Customer / SE | Scoped key for integration tests; rotate after onboarding |
| VPC Peering | Conditional | SE / Infra | Required for Private deployments; allow 10.0.0.0/16 from customer CIDR |
| TLS & Certs | Conditional | Customer / Infra | Customer-supplied certs allowed for on-prem gateway |
| KMS Integration | Conditional | Security / SE | Validate CMK access during provisioning |

Common known issues & recommended workarounds:
1) Symptom: Tokenization discrepancy / unexpected token counts
   - Root causes: Different tokenizer versions or preprocessing on customer side.
   - Workaround: Provide canonical tokenizer library (tokenizer v2.1) and sample script. Ask customer to send raw input and tokenized output.
   - Escalation: If model output quality is impacted, tag as P2 and involve Applied ML.

2) Symptom: Increased 5xx errors during high concurrency
   - Root causes: Autoscaling lag, batch queue overflow, or model OOMs (GPU memory).
   - Workaround: Recommend temporary throttling on client side and enable fallback model (smaller variant) in routing policy. Steps: update route to model-smaller-v1, set burst capacity to 2x for 30 minutes.
   - Commands: curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood.ai/v1/routes/<route_id> -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SE_KEY>' -d '{"fallback_model":"model-smaller-v1"}'

3) Symptom: Authentication failures (401) for valid keys
   - Root causes: Key rotation mismatch or clock skew on client.
   - Workaround: Verify key in console, restart client service, check system clock (NTP). If using short-lived credentials, confirm refresh flow.

4) Symptom: Persistent high latency (p95 > SLA)
   - Root causes: Long context lengths, lack of KV cache hits, misconfigured batching.
   - Workaround: Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, configure smaller batch windows for latency-sensitive routes. Provide sample yaml config and recommended thresholds.

Support process & triage (ticket flow):
1) Triage in Support queue (Tier 1):
   - Confirm customer, environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and reproduce issue.
   - Collect: request_id, timestamp, route_id, model, prompt_sample, logs, and a HAR or curl.
2) If not resolved within 4 hours or severity is P1/P0, escalate to Tier 2 (SE/Oncall SRE).
3) For code/regression issues, open an internal incident in Jira and link to the ticket.

Severity definitions & SLA targets:
| Severity | Definition | Initial response SLA | Target resolution | Escalation path |
|----------|------------|----------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| P0 (Critical) | Platform-wide outage affecting > 80% customers or data loss | 15 minutes | 4 hours | PagerDuty -> SRE -> Eng Director |
| P1 (High) | Single enterprise customer unusable (production blocking) | 30 minutes | 24 hours | Support -> Oncall SRE -> SE -> Product |
| P2 (Medium) | Feature degraded; workaround exists | 4 hours | 5 business days | Support -> SE |
| P3 (Low) | General question or minor bug | 48 hours | Product backlog cadence | Support |

Escalation matrix (quick reference):
- Step 0: CSM/Support acknowledges ticket to customer and collects required data within 1 hour.
- Step 1 (P1/P0): Trigger PagerDuty service redwood-inference-prod-oncall and post incident summary to #oncall-ops.
- Step 2: Oncall SRE performs initial mitigation (traffic routing, autoscaler adjustments, model fallback).
- Step 3: If mitigation requires code change, open an internal Jira and assign to Eng owner.
- Step 4: CSM coordinates customer comms and post-incident review.

Runbook: Immediate steps for P1 incident (step-by-step):
1) Acknowledge and triage (support Tier 1) — collect request_id, route_id, timestamps, sample prompts.
2) Reproduce: Attempt to reproduce in a test environment. If reproducible, capture full server logs.
3) Mitigate: Apply routing fallback to compatible model or scale up Dedicated pool. Example command: kubectl scale deployment/<inference-deployment> --replicas=3 (Private/Dedicated only).
4) Monitor: Watch p95 latency, error rate, and GPU utilization for 30 minutes. If error rate not decreasing, escalate to Eng on-call.
5) Communicate: CSM provides hourly status updates to customer until resolution.

Postmortem & regression triage:
- Post-incident, the owning team must publish a 1-pager in Confluence within 3 business days including timeline, root cause, impact, and action items. Link to: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems
- If regression impacts model quality, create an Eval case in applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage and add to the next model-release gating checklist.

QBR & Health check framework (90-day onboarding cadence):
1) 7-day health check (automated): provisioning, API key validation, and smoke tests.
2) 30-day check (CSM touch): usage baseline, latency metrics, initial integration issues, and feature enablement.
3) 60-day check (SE review): configuration optimization (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).
4) 90-day QBR — agenda:
   - Adoption metrics: active routes, daily token volume, top routes by tokens
   - Reliability: uptime (target 99.95%), p95 latency per route, error budget consumption
   - Cost and economics: average cost per 1k tokens, suggested batching/quantization changes to reduce unit cost
   - Quality: top 3 quality regressions, eval run status, and remediation plan
   - Roadmap & feature asks: next 90-day priorities for the customer
   - Action items and owners with deadlines

QBR deliverables (templates):
- Executive one-pager (PDF) with top KPIs
- Technical appendix with logs, top failing prompts, and configuration diffs
- Action tracker in shared Jira board with owner, due date, and status

Monitoring & dashboards to include in QBR:
- Per-route p95, p99 latency and throughput (tokens/s)
- Per-model error rate and 5xx breakdown
- Cost per 1k tokens and cost trend by route
- Cache hit rate and batch sizes

Appendix: Example escalation message (CSM -> #oncall-ops):
Subject: [P1] Customer AcmeCorp — model inference 5xx spike\nBody:
- Customer: AcmeCorp (enterprise)
- Environment: Dedicated (us-west-2, pool-id: d-42c4)
- Symptoms: 5xx rate increased from 0.2% to 12% since 2025-02-09 14:12 UTC
- Impact: Production traffic failing, estimated 90% of user flows affected
- Immediate steps taken: Enabled fallback model model-smaller-v1, throttled client to 60% of baseline
- Request: Oncall SRE to investigate autoscaler and GPU OOMs; SE to validate model memory profile
